function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

**How Turbonomic Helps Unilever Leverage AI‑Driven Multi‑Cloud Observability**

| What Turbonomic Provides | Why It Matters for Unilever |
|--------------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Unified Data Collection** – Ingests metrics, logs, events, and cost data from AWS CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, Google Cloud Operations Suite, Kubernetes, VMware vSphere, OpenShift, and even on‑premise systems. | Gives Unilever a single pane of glass for all workloads, eliminating siloed dashboards and manual data stitching. |
| **Real‑Time AI Analytics** – Uses machine‑learning models to continuously learn normal behavior, detect anomalies, and predict future capacity, performance, and cost trends. | Enables proactive issue resolution (auto‑remediation) and anticipates spikes before they hit production, keeping customer experience high while avoiding over‑provisioning. |
| **Policy‑Based Governance** – Define rules for cost caps, performance SLAs, compliance constraints, and sustainability targets. | Ensures every team follows corporate standards without needing separate teams to enforce them manually. |
| **Cross‑Cloud Optimization Engine** – Recommends optimal placement, sizing, and pricing options (reserved instances, spot/preemptible VMs, autoscaling groups, etc.) across AWS, Azure, GCP, and private clouds. | Cuts spend by up to 30–40 % (typical savings reported by Turbonomic customers) while maintaining or improving performance. |
| **Automated Remediation & Orchestration** – Executes actions such as moving workloads, resizing instances, or turning off idle resources through native APIs or Terraform/Ansible scripts. | Removes human error and speeds up response times from hours/days to minutes. |
| **Chargeback & Allocation** – Tags resources, attributes spend to business units, projects, or product lines, and generates drill‑down reports. | Gives finance and product managers clear visibility into who is using what, supporting better budgeting and ROI analysis. |
| **Root‑Cause Analysis & Predictive Insights** – Correlates performance, cost, and operational data to pinpoint the source of latency, cost spikes, or compliance gaps. | Reduces mean time to repair (MTTR) and prevents recurring incidents. |
| **Compliance & Security Integration** – Checks against PCI, GDPR, ISO 27001, and internal controls, and can trigger alerts or block deployments that violate policy. | Keeps Unilever compliant across all regions and reduces audit effort. |
| **Sustainability Metrics** – Calculates carbon footprints per workload and recommends greener instance types or regions. | Supports Unilever’s ESG goals and can be tied to executive KPIs. |

---

### Difference Between Turbonomic and Native Cloud Provider Tools

| Feature | Turbonomic | Native Cloud Tool (AWS CloudWatch / Azure Monitor / GCP Cloud Monitoring) |
|---------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Scope** | Cross‑cloud + on‑prem + container orchestration | Single‑cloud only |
| **Data Sources** | Aggregates metrics, logs, events, cost, and inventory from all clouds, Kubernetes clusters, VMware, etc. | Limited to the provider’s own services |
| **Analytics** | AI/ML‑driven predictions, anomaly detection, root‑cause analysis, capacity forecasting | Mostly rule‑based alerts, basic dashboards |
| **Optimization** | Automated recommendations for right‑size, placement, pricing, autoscaling, and migration | Manual tuning required; no cross‑cloud comparison |
| **Governance** | Policy engine that enforces cost, performance, compliance, and sustainability rules across all environments | Separate governance tools (e.g., AWS Config, Azure Policy) that work only within one cloud |
| **Automation** | Executes remediation actions via APIs, Terraform, Ansible, or native cloud SDKs | Requires custom scripting or third‑party tools |
| **Cost Attribution** | Built‑in chargeback, allocation, and forecasting across all clouds | Cost explorer per cloud; no unified view |
| **Dashboards** | Unified, customizable dashboards with cross‑cloud context | One dashboard per cloud; often need to stitch data manually |
| **Integration** | Works natively with Prometheus, Grafana, Splunk, ServiceNow, Jira, etc. | Integration usually requires additional connectors or manual export/import |
| **Speed of Insight** | Real‑time AI inference; near‑instant recommendations | Depends on log ingestion lag and manual analysis |
| **Vendor Lock‑In Mitigation** | Provides objective comparisons and migration paths | Each provider’s tools reinforce staying inside that ecosystem |

---

#### Bottom Line for Unilever

Turbonomic turns disparate cloud telemetry into actionable intelligence that spans all of Unilever’s public, private, and edge environments. By automating optimization, enforcing governance, and delivering unified observability, it lets Unilever:

* Reduce cloud spend while meeting or exceeding performance SLAs  
* Accelerate time‑to‑market for new products by freeing DevOps from manual tuning  
* Maintain compliance and security posture across global operations  
* Align IT spending with business value and sustainability goals  

Native cloud tools give you depth within a single provider, but Turbonomic gives you breadth, intelligence, and automation—exactly what a multinational consumer goods company needs to stay competitive in today’s multi‑cloud world.
